metadata.title: Mice with finitely many Woodin cardinals from optimal determinacy hypotheses

nodes.name: Gale-Stewart game $G(A)$
nodes.statement: For $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, $G(A)$ is the two-player game of length $\omega$ where players I and II alternately play $i_n \in \{0,1\}$; player I wins iff $(i_n)_{n<\omega} \in A$.

nodes.name: Determined game
nodes.statement: $G(A)$ (or $A$) is determined iff one of the players has a winning strategy in $G(A)$.

nodes.name: $A$-reflecting cardinal
nodes.statement: For cardinals $\kappa < \delta$ and $A \subseteq \delta$, $\kappa$ is $A$-reflecting in $\delta$ iff for every $\lambda < \delta$ there is a transitive model $M$ and elementary embedding $\pi: V \to M$ with $\mathrm{crit}(\pi)=\kappa$, $\pi(\kappa)>\lambda$ and $\pi(A) \cap \lambda = A \cap \lambda$.

nodes.name: Woodin cardinal
nodes.statement: A cardinal $\delta$ is a Woodin cardinal iff for all $A \subseteq \delta$ there is $\kappa < \delta$ which is $A$-reflecting in $\delta$.

nodes.name: Potential premouse
nodes.statement: $M$ is a potential premouse iff $M = (J_\eta^{\vec{E}}, \in, \vec{E}\restriction\eta, E_\eta)$ for some fine extender sequence $\vec{E}$ and ordinal $\eta$; $M$ is active iff $E_\eta \neq \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Premouse
nodes.statement: A potential premouse $M$ is a premouse iff every proper initial segment of $M$ is $\omega$-sound.

nodes.name: $\omega_1$-iterable premouse
nodes.statement: A premouse $M$ is $\omega_1$-iterable iff player II has a winning strategy in the iteration game $\mathcal{G}_\omega(M, \omega_1)$ as in Section 3.1 of Steel 2010.

nodes.name: $n$-small premouse
nodes.section: 1.3 Mice with Finitely Many Woodin Cardinals
nodes.statement: For $n \geq 1$, a premouse $M$ is $n$-small iff for every critical point $\kappa$ of an extender on the $M$-sequence, $M|\kappa \nvDash$ ``there are $n$ Woodin cardinals''. $M$ is $0$-small iff $M$ is an initial segment of $L$.

nodes.name: $M_n^\#(x)$
nodes.section: 1.3 Mice with Finitely Many Woodin Cardinals
nodes.statement: For $n \geq 1$ and $x \in {}^\omega\omega$, $M_n^\#(x)$ denotes the unique countable, sound, $\omega_1$-iterable $x$-premouse which is not $n$-small but all of whose proper initial segments are $n$-small, when it exists and is unique.

nodes.name: $M_n(x)$
nodes.section: 1.3 Mice with Finitely Many Woodin Cardinals
nodes.statement: Given $M_n^\#(x)$, $M_n(x)$ is the unique $x$-premouse obtained from $M_n^\#(x)$ by iterating its top measure out of the universe.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{Q}$-structure for $\mathcal{T}$
nodes.statement: For an iteration tree $\mathcal{T}$ on $N$ of limit length, $\mathcal{Q}=\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{T})$ is a $\mathcal{Q}$-structure iff $\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T}) \unlhd \mathcal{Q}$, $\delta(\mathcal{T})$ is a cutpoint, $\mathcal{Q}$ is $\omega_1$-iterable above $\delta(\mathcal{T})$, $\mathcal{Q} \vDash$ ``$\delta(\mathcal{T})$ is Woodin'' and a definability/projectum condition holds.

nodes.name: $\mathcal{Q}$-structure iteration strategy
nodes.statement: $\Sigma$ is the $\mathcal{Q}$-structure iteration strategy for $N$ iff $\Sigma(\mathcal{U})=b$ iff $\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{U})$ exists and $\mathcal{Q}(b,\mathcal{U})=\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{U})$.

nodes.name: $\delta$ not definably Woodin over $M$
nodes.statement: For a premouse $M$ and cardinal $\delta$ in $M$, $\delta$ is not definably Woodin over $M$ iff there is $\gamma$ with $\delta \le \gamma \le M\cap\mathrm{Ord}$ such that either an $r\Sigma_n$-definable set $A\subset\delta$ over $J_\gamma^M$ has no $\kappa<\delta$ strong up to $\delta$ w.r.t. $A$, or $\rho_n(J_\gamma^M)<\delta$.

nodes.name: $M_n^\#(N)$ (constructed on top of $N$)
nodes.statement: For a countable $x$-premouse $N$, $M_n^\#(N)$ is the smallest $x$-premouse $M \unrhd N$ with $\rho_\omega(M) \le N \cap \mathrm{Ord}$ which is $\omega_1$-iterable above $N \cap \mathrm{Ord}$, sound above $N\cap\mathrm{Ord}$, and either not fully sound or not $n$-small above $N\cap\mathrm{Ord}$.

nodes.name: Direct sum $x \oplus y$ and coding
nodes.statement: For $x=(x_n),y=(y_n)\in\BS$, $x \oplus y = (x_0,y_0,x_1,y_1,\dots)$. A real $x$ codes $M\oplus N$ iff $x \geq_T x_M \oplus x_N$ for codes $x_M,x_N$ of $M,N$.

nodes.name: Order $<_{\mathrm{OD}}$ on $\mathrm{OD}$-sets
nodes.statement: For $x,y\in\mathrm{OD}$ with minimal triples $(n,(\alpha_0,\dots,\alpha_n),\varphi)$ and $(m,(\beta_0,\dots,\beta_m),\psi)$, write $x<_{\mathrm{OD}} y$ iff the first triple precedes the second in the lexicographical order on triples.

nodes.name: $L[E](y)^M$ and iterated $L[E]$
nodes.statement: $L[E](y)^M$ is the result of a fully backgrounded extender construction above $y$ inside $M$ (with smallness weakened to allow $\omega$-small premice). $N$ is an iterated $L[E]$ in $M$ iff $N=M$ or $N$ is an iterated $L[E]$ in $L[E](z)^M$ for some $z\in M$ with $z\geq_T x$.

nodes.name: Equivalence $M \sim N$
nodes.statement: For premice $M,N$, $M\sim N$ iff $M$ and $N$ have the same sets of reals and the same $\mathrm{OD}$-sets of reals in the same order.

nodes.name: Pre-$n$-suitable premouse
nodes.statement: A countable premouse $N$ is pre-$n$-suitable iff there is $\delta<\omega_1^V$ with $N\vDash$``$\mathrm{ZFC}^- + \delta$ is the largest cardinal'', $N=M_{n-1}(N|\delta)|(\delta^+)^{M_{n-1}(N|\delta)}$, $M_{n-1}(N|\delta)$ is a proper class with $\delta$ Woodin, plus minimality and $\eta$-iterability conditions.

nodes.name: Short and maximal iteration tree
nodes.statement: A normal tree $\mathcal{T}$ on a pre-$n$-suitable $N$ below $\delta^N$ is short iff for every limit $\lambda<\mathrm{lh}(\mathcal{T})$ the $\mathcal{Q}$-structure $\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{T}\restriction\lambda)$ exists, is $(n-1)$-small above $\delta(\mathcal{T}\restriction\lambda)$ and $\unlhd\mathcal{M}_\lambda^{\mathcal{T}}$, with the analogous condition at $\mathrm{lh}(\mathcal{T})$ if limit; otherwise $\mathcal{T}$ is maximal.

nodes.name: Short tree iterable premouse
nodes.statement: A pre-$n$-suitable $N$ is short tree iterable iff for every short tree $\mathcal{T}$ on $N$, putative extensions have well-founded last models and (for limit length) there is a unique cofinal well-founded branch $b$ with $\mathcal{Q}(b,\mathcal{T})=\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{T})$.

nodes.name: $n$-suitable premouse
nodes.statement: A pre-$n$-suitable $N$ is $n$-suitable iff (i) $N$ is short tree iterable and short non-dropping iterates remain pre-$n$-suitable; and (ii) every maximal tree of limit length has a non-dropping cofinal well-founded branch $b$ with $\mathcal{M}_b^{\mathcal{T}}=M_{n-1}(\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T}))|(\delta(\mathcal{T})^+)^{M_{n-1}(\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T}))}$.

nodes.name: Lower part model $Lp^n(A)$
nodes.statement: For a countable transitive swo'd set $A$, $Lp^n(A)$ is the unique model of height $\omega_1^V$ obtained by iterating: at successor $\alpha+1$, $N_{\alpha+1}$ is the model-theoretic union of all countable $A$-premice $M\unrhd N_\alpha$ which are $n$-small above $N_\alpha\cap\mathrm{Ord}$, project to $\le N_\alpha\cap\mathrm{Ord}$, are sound and $\omega_1$-iterable above $N_\alpha\cap\mathrm{Ord}$, with $N_\alpha\cap\mathrm{Ord}$ a cutpoint.

nodes.name: Gale-Stewart open determinacy
nodes.statement: Assuming AC, every open or closed $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ has $G(A)$ determined.

nodes.name: Borel determinacy (Martin)
nodes.statement: Assuming AC, every Borel $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ has $G(A)$ determined.

nodes.name: Analytic determinacy from a measurable
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathrm{ZFC}$ and that there is a measurable cardinal. Then every analytic ($\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_1$) set of reals is determined.

nodes.name: Martin-Steel projective determinacy from Woodins
nodes.statement: For $n\geq 1$, if $\mathrm{ZFC}$ holds and there are $n$ Woodin cardinals with a measurable above them, then every $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_{n+1}$-definable set of reals is determined.
assumptions: $n$ Woodin cardinals exist with a measurable above them all

nodes.name: $\mathrm{AD}^{L(\mathbb{R})}$ from $\omega$ Woodins
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathrm{ZFC}$ and that there are $\omega$ Woodin cardinals with a measurable above them all. Then every set of reals in $L(\mathbb{R})$ is determined.
assumptions: $\omega$ Woodin cardinals with a measurable above

nodes.name: Harrington-Martin equivalence at $0^\#$
nodes.statement: Over $\mathrm{ZFC}$, $0^\#$ exists iff every $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1$-definable set of reals is determined.
conclusions: $0^\#$ exists $\iff$ every $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1$-set of reals is determined

nodes.name: Neeman's transfer theorem
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$ and assume $M_n^\#$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable. Then every $\game^{(n)}(<\omega^2-\Pi^1_1)$-definable set of reals is determined; in particular every $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_{n+1}$-set is determined.

nodes.name: Steel-Woodin equivalence at $M_1^\#$
nodes.statement: Over $\mathrm{ZFC}$, $M_1^\#$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable iff every $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1$- and every $\boldsymbol{\Delta}^1_2$-definable set of reals is determined.

nodes.name: $M_\omega^\#$ equivalence with $\mathrm{AD}^{L(\mathbb{R})}$
nodes.statement: Over $\mathrm{ZFC}$, $M_\omega^\#$ exists and is countably iterable iff $\mathrm{AD}^{L(\mathbb{R})}$ holds and $\mathbb{R}^\#$ exists.

nodes.name: Boldface Det-from-$M_n^\#(x)$ (cor:bfDetSharps)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$ and assume $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_{n+1}$ determinacy. Then $M_n^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all $x\in\BS$.

nodes.name: Lightface $M_n^\#$ existence (thm:newWoodin1)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$ and assume there is no $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_{n+2}$-definable $\omega_1$-sequence of pairwise distinct reals, and assume $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_n$ determinacy and $\Pi^1_{n+1}$ determinacy hold. Then $M_n^\#$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable.

nodes.name: Equivalence theorem (cor:newWoodin1)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 0$ and assume there is no $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_{n+2}$-definable $\omega_1$-sequence of pairwise distinct reals. Then the following are equivalent: (1) $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_n$ and $\Pi^1_{n+1}$ determinacy; (2) $M_{n-1}^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all $x$, and $M_n^\#$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable; (3) $M_n^\#$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable.

nodes.name: Steel: proper class model with $n$ Woodins (Steel)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$. If $M_{n-1}^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all $x\in{}^\omega\omega$ and all $\Sigma_{n+1}^1$-definable sets of reals are determined, then there exists a proper class inner model with $n$ Woodin cardinals.
assumptions: all $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$-definable sets of reals are determined
conclusions: there exists a proper class inner model with $n$ Woodin cardinals

nodes.name: $\omega_2$ is strongly inaccessible in HOD
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$. Assume $M_{n-1}^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all $x\in{}^\omega\omega$ and that all $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$-definable sets of reals are determined. Then for a cone of reals $x$, $\omega_2^{M_{n-1}(x)}$ is strongly inaccessible in $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x}$.
assumptions: all $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$-definable sets of reals are determined
conclusions: for a cone of $x$, $\omega_2^{M_{n-1}(x)}$ is strongly inaccessible in $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x}$

nodes.name: Generation Theorem (KW10)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$. Under the same hypotheses, for a cone of reals $x$, $\omega_2^{M_{n-1}(x)}$ is a Woodin cardinal in $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x}$.

nodes.name: Theorem newWoodinodd
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$. Assume every $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_{2n-1}$- and every $\Pi^1_{2n}$-definable set of reals is determined and there is no $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_{2n+1}$-definable $\omega_1$-sequence of pairwise distinct reals. Then $M_{2n-1}^\#$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable.

nodes.name: Theorem newWoodineven
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$ and assume there is no $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_{2n+2}$-definable $\omega_1$-sequence of pairwise distinct reals, and assume $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_{2n}$ determinacy and $\Pi^1_{2n+1}$ determinacy hold. Then $M_{2n}^\#$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable.

nodes.name: Determinacy Transfer Theorem (lightface)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$. Assume determinacy for every $\Pi^1_{2n-1}$- and $\Pi^1_{2n}$-definable set of reals. Then determinacy holds for all $\game^{(2n-1)}(<\omega^2-\Pi^1_1)$-definable sets of reals.

nodes.name: $\omega_2^{\bar{M}_z}$ inaccessible in HOD (varw2inacc)
nodes.statement: An analogue of $\omega_2$-inaccessibility in $\mathrm{HOD}$ adapted to the lower-part setting used in the even case.

nodes.name: Boldface relativized equivalence (cor:newWoodin1rel)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 0$. Then $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_{n+1}$ determinacy is equivalent to: for all $x\in\BS$, $M_n^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable.

nodes.name: Boldface Determinacy Transfer Theorem (cor:transferThm)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$. Then $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_{n+1}$ determinacy is equivalent to $\game^{(n)}(<\omega^2-\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_1)$ determinacy.

nodes.name: $\omega_1$ measurable in HOD (cor:w1)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$. Assume $M_{n-1}^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all $x\in{}^\omega\omega$ and all $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$-definable sets of reals are determined. Then $\omega_1^{M_{n-1}(x)}$ is measurable in $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x}$ for a cone of reals $x$.
assumptions: all $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$-definable sets of reals are determined
conclusions: for a cone of $x$, $\omega_1^{M_{n-1}(x)}$ is measurable in $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x}$

nodes.name: Absoluteness of short tree iterability (cor:absoluteness)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 0$, assume $M_{2n}^\#(x)$ exists for all $x\in\BS$ and let $N$ be pre-$(2n+1)$-suitable. Then $N$ is short tree iterable iff $N$ is short tree iterable inside $M_{2n}(N|\delta_N)^{\mathrm{Col}(\omega,\delta_N)}$.

nodes.name: Coiteration without definable Woodins (cor:itKS)
nodes.statement: Strengthening of Lemma itKS replacing 'no definable Woodin cardinals' with 'no Woodin cardinals'.

nodes.name: Game-quantifier transfer corollary (cor:transferthm)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$. Assume $\Pi^1_{2n-1}$ and $\Pi^1_{2n}$ determinacy. Suppose $Q\subseteq\BS$ is defined by a formula $\phi$ such that $x\in Q \iff M_{2n-2}(x)\vDash\phi(x,E,\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_m)$ for the extender sequence $E$ and first $m$ indiscernibles. Then $Q$ is determined.

nodes.name: Correctness of $M_n^\#(x)$ (lem:corr)
nodes.section: 1.3 Mice with Finitely Many Woodin Cardinals
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 0$ and assume $M_n^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all $x\in\BS$. (1) If $n$ even: $M_n^\#(x)$ is $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_{n+2}$-correct in $V$. (2) If $n$ odd: $\varphi(a)\iff\Vdash^{M_n^\#(x)}_{\mathrm{Col}(\omega,\delta_0)}\varphi(a)$ for $\Sigma^1_{n+2}$-formulas, and $M_n^\#(x)$ is $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_{n+1}$-correct in $V$.

nodes.name: Countable correctness (lem:ctblcorr)
nodes.section: 1.3 Mice with Finitely Many Woodin Cardinals
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 0$ and let $M$ be a countable $x$-premouse with $n$ Woodin cardinals such that $M\vDash\mathrm{ZFC}^-$ and $M$ is $\omega_1$-iterable. Periodic correctness holds for $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$-formulas.

nodes.name: Odd-case non-correctness (lem:oddnotcorr)
nodes.section: 1.3 Mice with Finitely Many Woodin Cardinals
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$ be odd and assume $M_n^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all $x\in\BS$. Then $M_n^\#(x)$ is not $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_{n+2}$-correct in $V$.

nodes.name: Kechris-Solovay generalization (lem:KS)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$. Assume $M_{n-1}^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all $x\in\BS$ and that all $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$-definable sets of reals are determined. Then there exists $y_0\in\BS$ such that for all $x\geq_T y_0$, $M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x \vDash \mathrm{OD}\text{-determinacy}$.
assumptions: all $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$-definable sets of reals are determined
conclusions: $\exists y_0\in\BS$ such that for all $x\geq_T y_0$, $M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x\vDash\mathrm{OD}\text{-determinacy}$

nodes.name: Q-structure uniqueness (lem:Qstrunique)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$ and assume $M_n^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all reals $x$. For an $n$-small $N$ and tree $\mathcal{T}$, the branch $b$ with $\mathcal{Q}(b,\mathcal{T})=\mathcal{Q}(\mathcal{T})$ is unique.

nodes.name: Iterability/comparison (lem:iterability)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$ and assume $M_{n-1}^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all reals $x$. For countable premice $M,N$ with common cutpoint $\delta$ that have no definable Woodin cardinals above $\delta$ and whose proper initial segments are $(n-1)$-small above $\delta$, parts (1)-(4) hold including closure of $H_{\delta_x}^{M_{n-1}^\#(x)}$ under $a\mapsto M_{n-2}^\#(a)$, internalization of iteration strategies, and successful comparison.
assumptions: $M_{n-1}^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all reals $x$
$M,N$ countable premice with common cutpoint $\delta$, $(n-1)$-small above $\delta$, no definable Woodins above $\delta$
conclusions: closure under $M_{n-2}^\#$ operation; iteration strategy is internal to $M_{n-1}^\#(x)|\delta_x$; comparison is successful

nodes.name: Steel's Lemma 2.2 generalization (lem:steel2.2)
nodes.statement: Generalization of Steel 1995 Lemma 2.2 to $\omega_1$-iterability for $(n-1)$-small comparable premice; allows $\Pi^1_n$-iterability on one side.

nodes.name: No fake Woodin / odd case (lem:nofakeeven)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$ odd, assume $M_{n-1}^\#(x)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all reals $x$. For $(n-1)$-small $\Pi^1_n$-iterable $M$ and $\omega_1$-iterable $N$ which is not $(n-1)$-small, with $M|\delta=N|\delta$, then $M\unlhd N$.

nodes.name: Coiteration without definable Woodins (lem:itKS)
nodes.statement: Variant of Lemma steel2.2 enabling successful coiteration of $(n-1)$-small premice with no definable Woodin cardinals via the existence of $\mathcal{Q}$-structures.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{OD}$-set agreement (lemma1und2)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 2$ and assume $M_{n-1}^\#(z)$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable for all $z\in\BS$. For $x\leq_T y$ and $M$ a $y$-premouse which is an iterated $L[E]$ in $M_{n-1}(x)$: (a) $M$ is $(n-1)$-small; (b) $M$ and $M_{n-1}(x)$ have the same sets of reals and the same $\mathrm{OD}$-sets in the same order.

nodes.name: Projectum lemma (lemma3)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 2$, $M_{n-1}^\#$ exist for all reals, $x\leq_T y$, $M$ an iterated $L[E]$ in $M_{n-1}(x)$ with least Woodin $\delta=\delta_M$, and a fully backgrounded extender construction sequence $(\mathcal{M}_\xi,\mathcal{N}_\xi)$ inside $M$ above $z\in M\cap\BS$ with $z\geq_T y$. Then for all $\xi\geq\delta$, $\rho_\omega(\mathcal{M}_\xi)\geq\delta$, hence $\mathcal{M}_\delta=L[E](z)|\delta$.

nodes.name: $\Sigma^1_{n+2}$-sequences are countable (lem:bfDetSeq)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 0$. Then $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_{n+1}$ determinacy implies that every $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_{n+2}$-definable sequence of pairwise distinct reals is countable.
conclusions: every $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^1_{n+2}$-definable $\omega_1$-sequence of distinct reals is countable

nodes.name: Existence of pre-$n$-suitable premouse (lem:prensuitable)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$. Assume $M_{n-1}^\#(x)$ exists for all $x\in{}^\omega\omega$ and that all $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$-definable sets of reals are determined. Then there exists a pre-$n$-suitable premouse.
assumptions: all $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$-definable sets of reals are determined

nodes.name: Weak Condensation Lemma (lem:weakcond)
nodes.statement: Let $N$ be pre-$n$-suitable with largest cardinal $\delta_N$, $\gamma$ large enough countable, and $H$ the Mostowski collapse of $\mathrm{Hull}_m^{M_{n-1}(N|\delta_N)|\gamma}(\{\delta_N\})$ for large $m$. Then $H \lhd M_{n-1}(N|\delta_N)$.

nodes.name: $\Pi^1_{2n+2}$-definability of short tree iterability (lem:defstiodd)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 0$ and assume $M_{2n}^\#(x)$ exists for all $x\in\BS$. For $N$ pre-$(2n+1)$-suitable, the statement '$N$ is short tree iterable' is $\Pi^1_{2n+2}$-definable uniformly in any code for $N$.

nodes.name: Pre-$(2n+1)$-suitable is $(2n+1)$-suitable (lem:nsuitnew)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 0$ and assume $M_{2n}^\#(x)$ exists for all $x\in\BS$. Then every pre-$(2n+1)$-suitable premouse is $(2n+1)$-suitable.

nodes.name: Collapse-correctness for $(2n+1)$-suitable (lem:colcorr)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 0$, $z\in\BS$, assume $M_{2n}^\#(x)$ exists for all $x\in\BS$ and $N$ a $(2n+1)$-suitable $z$-premouse. For any $\Sigma^1_{2n+3}$-formula $\varphi$ and $a\in N\cap\BS$: $\varphi(a) \iff \Vdash^N_{\mathrm{Col}(\omega,\delta_N)}\varphi(a)$.

nodes.name: Lower part well-defined (lem:LpWD)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$ and assume $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_{2n}$ determinacy. For any $x\in\BS$, the lower part model $Lp^{2n-1}(x)$ is well-defined as an $x$-premouse.

nodes.name: Lower part = iterate (lem:LpM)
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 1$ and assume $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_{2n}$ determinacy. For $x\in\BS$ and $M$ the $\omega_1^V$-th iterate of $M_{2n-1}^\#(x)$ by its least measure and its images: $M|\omega_1^V = Lp^{2n-1}(x)$.

nodes.name: Proof of correctness lemma
nodes.section: 1.3 Mice with Finitely Many Woodin Cardinals
nodes.statement: Simultaneous induction on $n$. Base $n=0$: Shoenfield absoluteness applied to the iterated top-measure model. Inductive step proves (1) and (2) for $n$ assuming both for $m<n$, distinguishing parity, using Neeman 1995 Cor. 1.8 to make a witness generic and the homogeneity of $\mathrm{Col}(\omega,\delta_0)$.

nodes.name: Base case $n=0$ via Shoenfield
nodes.statement: For $n=0$ apply Shoenfield's absoluteness theorem to the model obtained by iterating the top measure of $M_0^\#(x)$ until height $\geq \omega_1^V$; this model has the same reals as $M_0^\#(x)$.

nodes.name: Set up induction
nodes.statement: Simultaneously prove (1) and (2) for all $n\geq 1$ by induction; in fact the more general statement applies to any $n$-iterable $z$-premouse $N$ with $n$ Woodin cardinals countable in $V$.

nodes.name: Proof of (2) downward implication, $n$ odd
nodes.statement: For $\varphi(a)\equiv\exists x\forall y\,\psi(x,y,a)$ holding in $V$, fix witness $\bar{x}\in V$, use Neeman 1995 Cor. 1.8 to make $\bar{x}$ generic over an iterate $M^*$ of $M_n^\#(z)$ for $\mathrm{Col}(\omega,\delta_0)$, identify $M^*[g]=M_{n-1}^\#(z\oplus\bar{x})$, apply IH for $n-1$ ($\Sigma^1_n$-correctness) and homogeneity of the forcing; transfer back via elementarity.

nodes.name: Proof of (2) upward implication, $n$ odd
nodes.statement: Pick a $\mathrm{Col}(\omega,\delta_0)$-generic $g\in V$ over $M_n^\#(z)$ and a witness $\bar{x}\in V$ in $M_n^\#(z)[g]$; apply IH (1) for $n-1$ even to the formula $\forall y\,\psi(\bar{x},y,a)$.

nodes.name: Proof of (1) for $n$ even
nodes.statement: Use Moschovakis' Second Periodicity Theorem to uniformize $\Pi^1_{n+1}(a)$ giving a real $\bar{x}$ with $\{\bar{x}\}\in\Pi^1_{n+1}(a)$; relate via $\rho$, make $\bar{x}$ generic in an iterate $M^*$, apply IH (2) at level $n-1$ odd to the $\Pi^1_{n+1}$ formula $\rho(\bar{x},a)\wedge\forall y\,\psi(\bar{x},y,a)$, use homogeneity to bring witness into ground $M^*$.

nodes.name: Conclude (1) upward via downward
nodes.statement: Suppose $M_n^\#(z)\vDash\exists x\forall y\,\psi$ via $\bar{x}\in M_n^\#(z)$. If $V\nvDash\forall y\,\psi(\bar{x},y,a)$ then $V\vDash\exists y\,\neg\psi$ ($\Sigma^1_{n+1}$); applying the just-proved downward implication to this formula yields a contradiction.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma KS (Kechris-Solovay generalization)
nodes.statement: By contradiction at level $n>1$: cofinally many $y$ have $M\unlhd M_{n-1}(y)|\delta_y$ with $M\vDash\neg\mathrm{OD}\text{-det}$. Define properties (1)-(4) on $x$-premice $M$, show such $M$ exists on a Turing cone, build the generalized Kechris-Solovay game $G$, use winning strategies to derive that the least non-determined $\mathrm{OD}$-set in some $z$-premouse $N$ is determined, contradicting choice of $A_N$.

nodes.name: Reduction to $n>1$
nodes.statement: For $n=1$ the lemma follows from Theorem 3.1 of Kechris-Solovay 1985. Assume $n>1$ and suppose toward contradiction no such base real $y_0$ exists.

nodes.name: Set up properties (1)-(4) and Claim lemma4
nodes.statement: Define properties (1)-(4) on $x$-premice. Claim lemma4: for cofinally many $x$, $M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x$ satisfies (1) and (2). This uses Lemma lemma1und2 and Lemma lemma3 to verify the closure formula in (1).

nodes.name: Apply $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$ Turing-determinacy to get cone
nodes.statement: The set $A=\{x: \exists$ $x$-premouse $M$ with (1)-(4)$\}$ is $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$-definable and Turing-invariant; by determinacy it contains a cone with base $v$.

nodes.name: Comparison claim and iterability claim cl:it
nodes.statement: Show that an $x$-premouse $N$ satisfying (1)-(4) cannot win comparison against an $\omega_1$-iterable $M$ satisfying (1) and (2); conclude that $N$ is itself $\omega_1$-iterable. Hence cofinally many $x$ have every $x$-premouse with (1)-(4) being $\omega_1$-iterable.

nodes.name: Build the Kechris-Solovay-style game $G$
nodes.statement: Define $G$ where I plays $x\oplus a$, II plays $y\oplus b$; I wins iff some $(x\oplus y)$-premouse $M$ satisfies (1)-(4) and $a\oplus b\in A_M$ (the least $\mathrm{OD}$-set not determined in $M$). $G$ is $\Sigma^1_{n+1}$ and hence determined.

nodes.name: Construct minimizer with property $(3^*)$
nodes.statement: Pick $z^*\geq_T x_\tau\oplus v$ in cone, repeatedly minimize via $L[E](y_i)$-construction inside the witness $M^0$; descending chain of ordinals must terminate at finite $n$ giving $z=y_{n-1}$, $N=M^n$ with property $(3^*)$.

nodes.name: Player I winning case: build $\tau^*$ for $G(A_N)$
nodes.statement: Use I's winning strategy $\tau$ in $G$ to define $\tau^*$ for $G(A_N)$ inside $N$. Show $A_N=A_{N'}$ via the relations $L[E](x\oplus(z\oplus b))^N\sim N$, mouse-order $\le^*$ comparison, and minimality $(3^*)$.

nodes.name: Player II winning case: build $\sigma^*$ for $G(A_N)$
nodes.statement: Symmetric argument when II has winning strategy $\sigma$: define $\sigma^*$ for $G(A_N)$ with response $b=\sigma((z\oplus a)\oplus a)$; show $A_N=A_{N'}$ for $N'=L[E]((z\oplus a)\oplus y)^N$ giving determinacy of $A_N$ in $N$.

nodes.name: Conclude contradiction
nodes.statement: In both cases the least non-determined $\mathrm{OD}$-set $A_N$ is in fact determined inside $N$, contradicting the choice of $A_N$. Hence no failure premouse exists and Lemma KS holds.

nodes.name: Proof of Steel's proper class theorem
nodes.statement: Three-case analysis of the $K^c$-construction inside $M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x$. Case 1 ($K^c$ no Woodin, fully iterable): use Corollary cor:w1 to get $\omega_1$ measurable in HOD with $\omega_1=(\alpha^+)^K$, contradiction. Case 2 ($K^c$ has Woodin $\delta$): if $\delta$ stays Woodin in $L[E]$ above $K^c|\delta$ we get the desired model; else use definable-Woodin failure to derive contradiction via universality. Case 3 (no Woodin in $K^c$, not fully iterable): tree $\mathcal{T}$ has $\delta(\mathcal{T})$ Woodin in $L[E](\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T}))^{M_{n-1}(x)}$, giving the desired proper class model with $n$ Woodin cardinals.

nodes.name: Case 1: $(K^c)^{M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x}$ has no Woodin and is fully iterable
nodes.statement: Isolate core model $K^{M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x}$, weak covering forces $(\alpha^+)^K=\alpha^+$ for singular $\alpha=\aleph_\omega^{M_{n-1}(x)}$. After collapsing $\alpha$ generically over $M_{n-1}(x)$ and applying $\mathrm{OD}$-determinacy via Corollary cor:w1, obtain $\omega_1$ measurable in HOD with $\omega_1=(\alpha^+)^K=(\alpha^+)^{\mathrm{HOD}}$ contradicting $\mathrm{HOD}\vDash\mathrm{AC}$.

nodes.name: Case 2: Woodin in $K^c$
nodes.statement: Assume largest Woodin $\delta$ in $K^c$, with $K^c$ $(n-1)$-small above $\delta$. Perform $L[E]$-construction above $K^c|\delta$. Subcase 2.1: $\delta$ remains Woodin in resulting model $\Rightarrow$ proper class model with $n$ Woodins. Subcase 2.2: minimal $\xi$ with $\delta$ not definably Woodin over $\mathcal{M}_{\xi+1}$ $\Rightarrow$ coiterate $\mathcal{M}_{\xi+1}$ with $K^c$ inside $M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x$ via Claim cl:coitsucc; universality gives contradiction with non-Woodinness over $\mathcal{M}_{\xi+1}$.

nodes.name: Case 3: $K^c$ no Woodin, not fully iterable
nodes.statement: Failure of Q-structure iteration produces tree $\mathcal{T}$ on $K^c$ with no Q-structure inside $M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x$. $L[E]$-construction above $\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T})$ gives either (3.1) $\delta(\mathcal{T})$ Woodin and proper class model with $n$ Woodins, or (3.2) some $\mathcal{M}_{\xi+1}$ provides a Q-structure for $\mathcal{T}$ inside $M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x$, contradicting failure.

nodes.name: Proof of pre-$(2n+1)$-suitable is $(2n+1)$-suitable
nodes.statement: Toward contradiction take a witness tree $\mathcal{T}$. Pull back via Mostowski hull $\bar{W}\overset{\sigma}{\cong}\mathrm{Hull}^{W|\theta}_m(\{\delta_N\})\prec W|\theta$; Weak Condensation gives $\bar{W}\lhd W$. Encode failure as $\Sigma^1_{2n+2}$ statement $\phi$, transfer to $\bar{W}[g]$ via correctness, then derive contradictions through Q-structure / branch absoluteness in three cases (short-witness, short non-suitable iterate, maximal).

nodes.name: Set up Mostowski hull and Weak Condensation
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathcal{T}$ witnesses $N$ not $(2n+1)$-suitable. Pick $m,\theta$ large, let $\bar{W}$ be Mostowski collapse of $\mathrm{Hull}^{W|\theta}_m(\{\delta_N\})$ for $W=M_{2n}(N|\delta_N)$. Weak Condensation Lemma weakcond gives $\bar{W}\lhd W$ with $\rho_{m+1}(\bar{W})=\omega$.

nodes.name: Case 1: short tree witnesses non-iterability
nodes.statement: Build $\Sigma^1_{2n+2}$ statement $\phi_1(N)$ via Q-structure quantifications. Its negation in $\bar{W}[g]$ contradicts (using $\Sigma^1_{2n+1}$-correctness) the lack of cofinal branch through $\bar{\mathcal{T}}$ via subcases 1.1.1/1.1.2 (Woodin elementarity vs ordinal contradictions) and 1.2 (Q-structure exists below).

nodes.name: Case 2: short non-dropping iterate not pre-suitable
nodes.statement: Build $\Sigma^1_{2n+2}$ statement $\phi_2(N)$ asserting existence of premouse $\mathcal{P}$ above $\mathcal{M}_\lambda^\mathcal{T}|\delta_{\mathcal{M}_\lambda^\mathcal{T}}$ over which $i_{0\lambda}^\mathcal{T}(\delta_N)$ is not definably Woodin. Coiterate inside $W$ using Steel's Lemma 2.2; cases 2.1/2.2 give contradictions.

nodes.name: Case 3: maximal tree without good branch
nodes.statement: $\Sigma^1_{2n+2}$ statement $\phi_3(N)$ using $\mathcal{P}\rhd\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T})$ playing the role of a Q-structure with $\delta(\mathcal{T})$ Woodin. Subcases 3.1 (drop on branch) and 3.2 (no drop, with 3.2.1/3.2.2) close via $\Sigma^1_1$-absoluteness and ordinal counting.

nodes.name: Conclude pre-suitability of iterates
nodes.statement: From the contradictions in Cases 2 and 3, conclude $M_{2n}(\mathcal{M}_\lambda^\mathcal{T}|\delta_{\mathcal{M}_\lambda^\mathcal{T}})\vDash$ ``$\delta_{\mathcal{M}_\lambda^\mathcal{T}}$ Woodin'' in Case 2 and $\mathcal{M}_b^\mathcal{T}=M_{2n}(\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T}))|(\delta(\mathcal{T})^+)^{M_{2n}(\mathcal{M}(\mathcal{T}))}$ in Case 3; properties (1)-(4) of pre-$(2n+1)$-suitability transfer.

nodes.name: Proof of bfDetSeq lemma
nodes.statement: Suppose toward contradiction $\leq^*$ is a $\Sigma^1_{n+2}$-definable well-order of order type $\omega_1$. By $\Pi^1_{n+1}$ determinacy, $\Sigma^1_{n+2}$ has the perfect set property, so $X_{\leq^*}$ has perfect subset $P$. Iteratively use Claim cl:bfDetSeq to build descending chain $f_{n+1}(x)<^*f_n(x)$ on $\bigcap P_n\neq\emptyset$, contradicting well-foundedness.

nodes.name: Reduce via perfect set property
nodes.statement: From $\Pi^1_{n+1}$ determinacy obtain perfect set property for $\Sigma^1_{n+2}$, hence perfect $P\subseteq X_{\leq^*}$.

nodes.name: Claim: descend via continuous injection
nodes.statement: Claim cl:bfDetSeq: given perfect $P_0$ and continuous injection $f_0:P_0\to P$, find perfect $P_1\subseteq P_0$ and continuous injection $f_1:P_1\to P$ with $f_1(x)<^* f_0(x)$ on $P_1$.

nodes.name: Compactness and infinite descent contradiction
nodes.statement: Iterate the claim to get $(P_n)$ with $f_{n+1}(x)<^* f_n(x)$ on $P_{n+1}$; compactness of $2^\omega$ gives $\bigcap P_n\neq\emptyset$, yielding infinite $<^*$-descending chain, contradicting that $\leq^*$ is a well-order.

nodes.name: Claim lemma4: cofinally many witnesses for (1)+(2)
nodes.statement: For cofinally many $x\in\BS$, $M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x$ satisfies properties (1) and (2).

nodes.name: Claim cl:it: iterability for premice with (1)-(4)
nodes.statement: If there is an $\omega_1$-iterable $x$-premouse $M$ with properties (1) and (2), then every $x$-premouse $N$ with properties (1)-(4) is itself $\omega_1$-iterable.

nodes.name: Claim cl:tau*: $\tau^*$ wins $G(A_N)$
nodes.statement: $\tau^*$ is a winning strategy for player I in the Gale-Stewart game with payoff $A_N$ played in $N$.

nodes.name: Claim cl:sigma*: $\sigma^*$ wins $G(A_N)$
nodes.statement: $\sigma^*$ is a winning strategy for player II in the Gale-Stewart game with payoff $A_N$ played in $N$.

nodes.name: Claim cl:LEnsmall: $L[E]$ is $(n-1)$-small
nodes.statement: The $y$-premouse $M$ obtained as iterated $L[E]$ in $M_{n-1}(x)$ is $(n-1)$-small.

nodes.name: Claim cl:coitsucc: coiteration succeeds
nodes.statement: The coiteration of $\mathcal{M}_{\xi+1}$ and $(K^c)^{M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x}$ inside $M_{n-1}(x)|\delta_x$ is successful.

nodes.name: Claim cl:bfDetSeq: continuous descent claim
nodes.statement: Given perfect $P_0$ and continuous injection $f_0:P_0\to P$, there is a perfect $P_1\subseteq P_0$ and continuous injection $f_1:P_1\to P$ with $f_1(x)<^* f_0(x)$ for all $x\in P_1$.

nodes.name: Claim cl:QmphiDet: $Q^\phi_m$ determined
nodes.statement: For all formulas $\phi$ and all $m<\omega$, the set $Q^\phi_m=\{x: M_{2n-2}(N_x|\delta_{N_x})\vDash\phi(E,\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_m)\}$ is determined.

nodes.name: Lightface conjecture
nodes.statement: Let $n>1$ and assume $\boldsymbol{\Pi}^1_n$ determinacy and $\Pi^1_{n+1}$ determinacy hold. Then $M_n^\#$ exists and is $\omega_1$-iterable. (Open for $n>1$; known for $n=0$ and $n=1$.)

nodes.name: Periodicity necessitates split arguments
nodes.statement: The proofs of the odd and even levels of the projective hierarchy differ because of the periodicity in uniformization and correctness of $M_n^\#$.

nodes.name: Mouse order $\leq^*$
nodes.statement: $M\leq^* N$ iff $M$ and $N$ successfully coiterate to $M^*\unlhd N^*$ with no drops on the main branch from $M$ to $M^*$. Write $M=^* N$ iff both hold.
